question: What are the 10 most frequently reported HTL materials in n-i-p perovskite solar cells with PCE above 20%?
final_answer:
**Top 10 HTL entries in the n-i-p subset with JV_default_PCE > 20%** (counted from the `devices` table, `Cell_architecture` = nip, `HTL_stack_sequence` as the material field, PCE taken as `JV_default_PCE` and converted to % where stored as a fraction):

| # | HTL (exact string in `HTL_stack_sequence`) | Records with PCE > 20% | Total nip records for that entry |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Spiro-MeOTAD | 1010 | 20,924 |
| 2 | none (no HTL deposited) | 82 | 2,424 |
| 3 | PTAA | 47 | 990 |
| 4 | P3HT | 40 | 858 |
| 5 | PEAI \| Spiro-MeOTAD | 18 | 20 |
| 6 | CuSCN | 16 | 180 |
| 7 | TQ1 | 8 | 9 |
| 8 | DM | 7 | 12 |
| 9 | PEDOT | 4 | 39 |
| 10 | PDBD-T | 4 | 29 |

**Key points and caveats**

- Spiro-MeOTAD dominates: 1010 of the 1236 high-PCE n-i-p records in this top-10 list (≈81.7%); it is the only single-material HTL with four-digit counts.
- "none" is not a material — it marks devices with no HTL. If you want materials only, drop row 2; the sequence then becomes Spiro-MeOTAD (1010), PTAA (47), P3HT (40), PEAI | Spiro-MeOTAD (18), CuSCN (16), TQ1 (8), DM (7), then a 9-way tie at 4 records (PEDOT, PDBD-T, PMMA | Spiro-MeOTAD, CH3O-PEIA | Spiro-MeOTAD, DTP-C6Th, TPFPB | Spiro-MeOTAD, C6Br | Spiro-MeOTAD, SrCl2 | Spiro-MeOTAD, P(VDF-TrFE) | Spiro-MeOTAD). Ranks 9–10 are therefore arbitrary among that tie; PEDOT:PSS (3) and CuPc (3) sit just below.
- This is a ranking of *stack strings*, not isolated chemical species. Interlayers/dopants are stored as a " | " stack (e.g. PEAI | Spiro-MeOTAD, NiO-np | Meo-2PACz), so a material-by-material count would push Spiro-MeOTAD even higher; I did not run a string-splitting query, so that decomposition is not established here.
- Counts are device records, not deduplicated publications. Several rows per paper (and per paper/table-entry) appear to exist, so "most frequently reported" here means most frequently recorded, and per-paper frequency could order these differently.
- Data-quality flag: `max_pce` for several groups is 100.0, 99.0, 98.0, 86.0, 77.0, 71.0, 33.0 — i.e. some `JV_default_PCE` entries are 1.00 (or literal 100) sentinels/placeholders that my % conversion pushed above the 20% cut. A few rows per group are likely mis-binned; the magnitude gaps above are large enough that the top ordering is unlikely to change, but exact counts for the small-count entries (ranks 7–10) are less reliable.
- "material" appears in only one column name in this schema (`Encapsulation_edge_sealing_materials`), so `HTL_stack_sequence` is the sole HTL material field; HTL dopants/additives live separately in `HTL_additives_compounds` and were not counted as materials.
- Acronyms (TQ1, DM, DTP-C6Th, C6Br, PDBD-T) are reproduced exactly as spelled in the database; I did not expand them or verify their full chemical names in the literature.
- Not established: the total number of n-i-p records with PCE > 20% (the aggregate was not queried, only per-group counts for the top 20 groups), and per-reference (DOI-level) frequencies. The full nip subset contains 29,897 records.

**Top 10 HTL entries in the n-i-p subset with JV_default_PCE > 20%** (counted from the `devices` table, `Cell_architecture` = nip, `HTL_stack_sequence` as the material field, PCE taken as `JV_default_PCE` and converted to % where stored as a fraction):

| # | HTL (exact string in `HTL_stack_sequence`) | Records with PCE > 20% | Total nip records for that entry |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Spiro-MeOTAD | 1010 | 20,924 |
| 2 | none (no HTL deposited) | 82 | 2,424 |
| 3 | PTAA | 47 | 990 |
| 4 | P3HT | 40 | 858 |
| 5 | PEAI \| Spiro-MeOTAD | 18 | 20 |
| 6 | CuSCN | 16 | 180 |
| 7 | TQ1 | 8 | 9 |
| 8 | DM | 7 | 12 |
| 9 | PEDOT | 4 | 39 |
| 10 | PDBD-T | 4 | 29 |

**Key points and caveats**

- Spiro-MeOTAD dominates: 1010 of the 1236 high-PCE n-i-p records in this top-10 list (≈81.7%); it is the only single-material HTL with four-digit counts.
- "none" is not a material — it marks devices with no HTL. If you want materials only, drop row 2; the sequence then becomes Spiro-MeOTAD (1010), PTAA (47), P3HT (40), PEAI | Spiro-MeOTAD (18), CuSCN (16), TQ1 (8), DM (7), then a 9-way tie at 4 records (PEDOT, PDBD-T, PMMA | Spiro-MeOTAD, CH3O-PEIA | Spiro-MeOTAD, DTP-C6Th, TPFPB | Spiro-MeOTAD, C6Br | Spiro-MeOTAD, SrCl2 | Spiro-MeOTAD, P(VDF-TrFE) | Spiro-MeOTAD). Ranks 9–10 are therefore arbitrary among that tie; PEDOT:PSS (3) and CuPc (3) sit just below.
- This is a ranking of *stack strings*, not isolated chemical species. Interlayers/dopants are stored as a " | " stack (e.g. PEAI | Spiro-MeOTAD, NiO-np | Meo-2PACz), so a material-by-material count would push Spiro-MeOTAD even higher; I did not run a string-splitting query, so that decomposition is not established here.
- Counts are device records, not deduplicated publications. Several rows per paper (and per paper/table-entry) appear to exist, so "most frequently reported" here means most frequently recorded, and per-paper frequency could order these differently.
- Data-quality flag: `max_pce` for several groups is 100.0, 99.0, 98.0, 86.0, 77.0, 71.0, 33.0 — i.e. some `JV_default_PCE` entries are 1.00 (or literal 100) sentinels/placeholders that my % conversion pushed above the 20% cut. A few rows per group are likely mis-binned; the magnitude gaps above are large enough that the top ordering is unlikely to change, but exact counts for the small-count entries (ranks 7–10) are less reliable.
- "material" appears in only one column name in this schema (`Encapsulation_edge_sealing_materials`), so `HTL_stack_sequence` is the sole HTL material field; HTL dopants/additives live separately in `HTL_additives_compounds` and were not counted as materials.
- Acronyms (TQ1, DM, DTP-C6Th, C6Br, PDBD-T) are reproduced exactly as spelled in the database; I did not expand them or verify their full chemical names in the literature.
- Not established: the total number of n-i-p records with PCE > 20% (the aggregate was not queried, only per-group counts for the top 20 groups), and per-reference (DOI-level) frequencies. The full nip subset contains 29,897 records.
